sites.ownership: The close coordinator owns the active sequential close queue.
sites.justification: Unsaved tab-close, window-close, and quit flows need mutable queue progress without leaking state into the window shell.

sites.ownership: The document portal resolver owns the process-local document ID to host-path cache and in-flight callback queue.
sites.justification: Display-path rendering must not block the UI on portal D-Bus calls, so async GetHostPaths results are coalesced and cached while portal access paths remain authoritative for I/O.

sites.ownership: Each document monitor owns the removable polling source.
sites.justification: File-monitor events can be unreliable on portal-backed paths, so the binding keeps one cancellable polling source that is removed with the GIO monitor.

sites.ownership: Each document monitor owns one async file-stamp state machine.
sites.justification: GIO metadata queries complete asynchronously, so monitor events, polling fallback, cancellation, and stale-result guards must coalesce through one mutable state cell without blocking the GTK main loop.

sites.ownership: The search controller owns one mutable binding to the active tab and active search context.
sites.justification: Workspace-level search preserves query state while rebinding highlights, match counts, and replace state to the selected tab.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns one shared mutable state cell split into document runtime, IO, external-file, autosave, compare, and UI owner structs.
sites.justification: The tab facade coordinates cross-owner transitions such as writability, autosave pausing, banners, compare reference loading, and scratch-then-apply IO without introducing multiple independent RefCell borrows.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current workspace file-drop callback.
sites.justification: Tabs can move between windows, so file-drop routing must be replaceable without rebuilding the editor widget.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current workspace visual-state callback.
sites.justification: Cursor, dirty, and title updates must rebind to the destination workspace when a tab is transferred to another window.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current external-state callback.
sites.justification: External file-change banners must update the workspace that currently owns the tab after window transfer.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current external-action callback.
sites.justification: Reload, save, and compare banner actions must route to the workspace that currently owns the tab.

sites.ownership: Each compare controller owns the presentation metadata shared with its two read-only presentation panes.
sites.justification: Copy handlers need the current placeholder marker metadata after every recompute so generated marker text can be filtered without string matching.

sites.ownership: Presentation pane interactions borrow the controller-owned presentation metadata.
sites.justification: Selection copy must replace generated placeholder marker rows with blank text while preserving clipboard line layout.

sites.ownership: The window-owned zoom controller owns the resolved base editor font description.
sites.justification: Zoom and font changes need one mutable source of truth that can update all open tabs and the minimap without duplicating state per tab.

sites.ownership: The window-owned zoom controller owns the current zoom percentage for the whole workspace window.
sites.justification: Window-scoped zoom actions must clamp, reset, and reapply the same percentage across every attached editor tab.

sites.ownership: The project tree model owns shared lazy-loading state.
sites.justification: Directory enumeration, monitor callbacks, and refresh callbacks need a generation counter, hidden filter state, active root, cancellables, and directory monitors shared across tree expansions.

sites.ownership: Enumerator batching carries shared tree state across async callbacks.
sites.justification: Batch iteration needs generation checks, cancellable ownership, and monitor registration context without global variables.

sites.ownership: Directory-load helpers borrow shared tree model state.
sites.justification: Async enumeration must consult the current generation and hidden filter, then register directory monitors without racing root changes.

sites.ownership: Enumeration error handling uses shared tree state.
sites.justification: Error callbacks must ignore stale generations and update the correct list store without racing refresh operations.

sites.ownership: Each project directory monitor owns the removable polling source.
sites.justification: Portal-backed directory monitors can miss structural events, so loaded directories keep a cancellable snapshot polling source.

sites.ownership: Each project directory monitor owns a shared polling cancellation flag.
sites.justification: Async snapshot callbacks need a stale guard after root replacement, refresh, hidden-toggle refresh, or close-folder cancellation.

sites.ownership: The directory polling loop shares the last observed snapshot.
sites.justification: Loaded-directory polling compares child name/type snapshots without broad filesystem permissions or recursive watchers.

sites.ownership: The directory polling loop shares its cancellation flag.
sites.justification: Timeout callbacks must stop immediately after the directory monitor is cancelled by a generation change.

sites.ownership: Directory-poll callbacks carry shared snapshot state.
sites.justification: Async enumeration batches need access to the previous snapshot when deciding whether to trigger one coalesced tree refresh.

sites.ownership: Directory-poll callbacks carry the shared cancellation flag.
sites.justification: Late async enumeration completions must not refresh the current tree after their monitor generation has been cancelled.

sites.ownership: The directory polling loop shares its in-flight enumeration guard.
sites.justification: The timeout source must avoid overlapping directory enumerations on slow portal or network filesystems.

sites.ownership: The directory snapshot transition helper mutates shared polling state.
sites.justification: Snapshot comparison is centralized so root and loaded-dir polling trigger refreshes only on visible structural changes.

sites.justification: Preference callbacks need one syncing guard and staged numeric state so UI population and write-back do not recursively write settings.

sites.justification: Preferences initialization and sanitized write-back need one explicit guard that suppresses recursive signals without weakening GSettings timing rules.

sites.ownership: The staged SpinRow write helper mutates the shared preferences state.

sites.ownership: The window project controller owns shared project sidebar state.
sites.justification: Sidebar actions, async folder open/restore, refresh, and tab→tree reveal must coordinate through one mutable state cell.

sites.ownership: Tree activation wiring stores one late-bound handler closure.
sites.justification: Activation callbacks need the project state Rc after construction without creating a reference cycle between the tree and controller.

sites.ownership: Root-action synchronization borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Root transitions must consistently enable/disable window actions and sidebar visibility from one state source of truth.

sites.ownership: Project root transition helpers borrow shared project state.
sites.justification: Opening, restoring, replacing, and revealing project roots must coordinate cancellables, sidebar state, and tree synchronization from one state source.

sites.ownership: Root-change sidebar visibility borrows shared project state after mutation is complete.
sites.justification: Split-view notify handlers can re-enter project state, so visibility changes run after root mutation releases its mutable borrow.

sites.ownership: App-open handling borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: GApplication::open classification needs access to project state so a folder input can replace the active project root.

sites.ownership: App-open request processing borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Async file-type probes must enqueue follow-up callbacks against the same project state to apply root replacement and toasts safely.

sites.ownership: The app-open request accumulates classification results across async callbacks.
sites.justification: Mixed directory/file opens must collect results before deciding which folder to activate and which files to open as tabs.

sites.ownership: App-open finishing borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Completion logic needs shared access to the active workspace and toast overlay to apply the aggregated open decisions.

sites.ownership: The app-open finisher reads the accumulated request state.
sites.justification: Finishing needs the collected directory/file lists to open the first folder and then open any remaining files as tabs.

sites.ownership: The project auto-refresh coalescer owns the pending refresh flag.
sites.justification: Directory monitors can emit bursts across multiple folders, so the controller needs one shared pending flag to schedule at most one refresh per debounce window.

sites.ownership: Refresh handling borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Manual and monitor-triggered refresh need the active root, expansion snapshotting, and reveal coordination without spawning background threads.

sites.ownership: Symlink activation borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Symlink resolution needs cancellable state and toast deduplication shared with other sidebar operations.

sites.ownership: The workspace owns tab collection, recent/session caches, restore gating, and active close flow.
sites.justification: Tabbed document coordination requires shared mutable state across menu rebuilds, session persistence, search/status rebinding, selection changes, and drag-and-drop.

sites.ownership: The guarded autosave test request owns its observed asynchronous save result.
sites.justification: GTK regression coverage needs to prove the production autosave gate either skipped the write or returned the real save result without duplicating eligibility logic in the test.

sites.ownership: Each workspace owns the callback that creates registered destination windows for tab transfer.
sites.justification: The tab menu needs to create a secondary window through the app registry while avoiding a strong AppState cycle in workspace state.

sites.ownership: Each workspace owns the page currently being transferred out or in.
sites.justification: The detach handler must distinguish transfer from real close so file monitors and zoom styling are not cleared for moved tabs.

sites.ownership: The shared open-request state tracks a multi-file open batch.
sites.justification: Multi-open, restore, and drag-and-drop need sequential progress, success/failure counts, and selected-tab restoration across async callbacks.

sites.ownership: The open-request finisher reads shared batch state.
sites.justification: Completion handling needs the accumulated batch results to decide between restore selection, aggregated toasts, and fallback UI state.

sites.ownership: Project root finish helpers borrow shared project state after the mutable root update is released.
sites.justification: Finishing a root replacement must update the project tree outside the ProjectState mutable borrow while still reading the current browser owner.
